integrated_answer.claim: GET/POST /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/conversations/:conversation_id/labels map to index/create. The controller operates @conversation and permits conversation_id plus labels: [] (array). These visible strong parameters establish shape, not a label-title whitelist.

Before either action, lookup is Current.account.conversations.find_by!(display_id: params[:conversation_id]), followed by authorize @conversation, :show?. Accounts::BaseController invokes current_account and conditional token API-access/MFA guards; disabled API access renders forbidden. Complete helper/policy rules are outside this packet.

GET reads model.label_list. POST calls update_labels(permitted_params[:labels]), whose implementation is update!(label_list: labels), then reads label_list. It assigns rather than using add_labels, which explicitly combines labels. Both templates render {"payload": labels}.

POST expresses replacement semantics rather than append semantics. Exact normalization, callbacks, empty/missing-input behavior and resulting persisted values require the unlisted persistence implementation or runtime verification.

Account label CRUD is separately routed at /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/labels: index/show/create/update/destroy. It policy-scopes index, calls check_authorization, fetches account label records by id, and accepts nested label metadata title/description/color/show_on_sidebar. Destroy queues association removal. This differs from assigning a conversation's labels.

Existing request-test source has four examples: unauthenticated GET and POST expect unauthorized; same-account agent with inbox membership gets success, GET contains label1/label2 and POST contains label3/label4. These are source assertions, not execution results.
